title: Mushaf or printed al-Fath 48:1
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 2: The Prophet ﷺ as leader; Shahadah and Salah (1.7, 3.1, 3.2)
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y10 lesson 19 (Mushaf or printed al-Fath 48:1)
intro: Lesson 19: 1.7 Consolidation and expansion: treaties, conquest and the Year of Delegations. To understand how Islam was consolidated and expanded after the Hijrah

questions.q: Explain how the conquest of Makkah consolidated Islam. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: The Ka'bah was cleared of idols, the Quraysh's opposition ended, and Arabia's tribes saw Islam's strength and mercy, leading to the Year of Delegations.
questions.model: Point 1: it removed the main enemy. Develop: the Quraysh, leaders of opposition, accepted the Prophet ﷺ. Point 2: the Ka'bah returned to tawheed. Develop: the idols were destroyed (17:81: truth has come), making Makkah the centre of Islam.

questions.q: The Year of Delegations was in ...

Ranking task on the pupil PDF: rank five events (Charter, Hudaybiyyah, letters, conquest, delegations) by how much each expanded Islam, with a reason each; then a 'most important' paragraph in the portal response box.
questions.a: Reasoned ranking; paragraph with evidence (e.g. Hudaybiyyah via 48:1 and growth in peace)
questions.model: Teacher ranks Hudaybiyyah first and gives a reason: 'It brought peace, so many could hear Islam; Allah called it a clear victory (48:1).'

questions.q: why did the Prophet ﷺ write to rulers and not just send armies?
questions.a: Islam is spread by invitation; there is no compulsion in religion (2:256).

questions.q: link consolidation to the 12-mark statement on opponents and prisoners.
questions.a: Mercy at the conquest and in treaties won hearts, supporting the statement.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: can a treaty that looks like a loss be a victory?
questions.a: Yes: Hudaybiyyah's peace let Islam spread (48:1).
